# AI Agents

An AI agent is an actor whose handler calls a language model. Nothing else changes.

```{=html}
<div class="two-col">
  <div>
    <div class="card"><h3>Tool calling</h3><p>Tools are actors. Calling a tool means publishing to its topic. The result arrives as a new message on a subscribed topic.</p></div>
    <div class="card"><h3>Multi-round state</h3><p>Conversation history lives in LMDB <code>state/</code>, keyed by correlation ID. Each round picks up exactly where the last left off.</p></div>
  </div>
  <div>
    <div class="card"><h3>Agent chaining</h3><p>An agent publishes to another agent's topic. Supervisor, specialist, critic — all natural compositions on the same bus.</p></div>
    <div class="card"><h3>Fault isolation</h3><p>A crashing handler exits. The runtime survives. The next tuple spawns a fresh process. No shared heap, no corrupted state.</p></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## The ReAct Loop

ReAct — Reason + Act — is the standard agentic pattern: reason about what to do, call a tool, observe the result, iterate until done. On a mesh this loop is a **message flow**, not a control flow.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant C  as Client
  participant AG as Agent actor
  participant TL as Tool actor

  C  ->> AG : user_message {query}
  Note over AG: load history from LMDB[corr_id], call LLM with tools
  AG ->> TL : sql_query {sql}
  Note over TL: execute SQL, return rows or error
  TL ->> AG : sql_result {rows} or {error}
  Note over AG: append tool result, call LLM again
  AG ->> C  : agent_response {answer}
  Note over AG: persist updated history to LMDB[corr_id]
```

The agent actor subscribes to both `user_message` and `sql_result`. The bus does not care that the same actor receives both. The `correlation_id` in the tuple header ties separate invocations into one logical conversation — and keys the LMDB memory that carries history across turns.

Duplicate delivery is handled atomically: the handler writes `ACTOR_TUPLE_ID` into a `dedup` LMDB database with `MDB_NOOVERWRITE`. If the key already exists the handler exits silently with no output, and the runtime publishes nothing.

::: {.callout}
**The loop has no fixed depth.** An agent can emit `sql_query`, receive `sql_result`, emit another `sql_query`, and so on up to whatever bound the handler enforces. The runtime is oblivious — it just delivers tuples.
:::

## Multi-Agent Topology

```{mermaid}
stateDiagram-v2
  direction TB

  User        : user
  Supervisor  : supervisor agent
  DataAgent   : data agent
  CodeAgent   : code agent
  WebAgent    : web agent
  SQLTool     : sql tool
  PyRunner    : python runner
  WebFetch    : web fetch

  [*]         --> User
  User        --> Supervisor  : request

  Supervisor  --> DataAgent   : data_query
  Supervisor  --> CodeAgent   : code_task
  Supervisor  --> WebAgent    : web_task

  DataAgent   --> SQLTool     : sql_query
  SQLTool     --> DataAgent   : sql_result

  CodeAgent   --> PyRunner    : run_python
  PyRunner    --> CodeAgent   : run_result

  WebAgent    --> WebFetch    : fetch_url
  WebFetch    --> WebAgent    : fetch_result

  DataAgent   --> Supervisor  : data_result
  CodeAgent   --> Supervisor  : code_result
  WebAgent    --> Supervisor  : web_result

  Supervisor  --> User        : response
  User        --> [*]
```

Each box is an independent process. The supervisor has no imports from specialist code. Every edge is a topic on the bus.
